speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are presenting with hand tremors and recent memory issues; to better understand the underlying cause, could you tell me how long you have noticed these symptoms and if they are occurring at rest or while using your hands?

speaker: Patient
text: 70-year-old man accompanied by his wife. The patient first noticed the tremor in his left hand 1 year ago, which has been progressively worsening. Recently, he has faced difficulty in performing tasks that require steadiness, such as reading. His wife has observed a decline in his memory, taking note of his forgetfulness in paying bills, a task she has since had to assume.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed history. text: My main symptom is Resting tremor worse on the left hand. I also have Soft speech, Reduced facial expressions, Memory decline, Difficulty in managing finances.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Hypertension, medicated with aspirin and amlodipine. Family history of schizophrenia in his mother. No other significant medical or psychiatric history. Social history: Drinks 1-2 beers nightly and is a former cigar smoker.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies any other systemic complaints. Specifically, no urinary symptoms, no significant changes in bowel habits, no reported falls or dizziness. speaker: Doctor
text: The patient has denied urinary symptoms, bowel changes, or falls, which helps rule out normal pressure hydrocephalus. The combination of asymmetric resting tremor, soft speech, reduced facial expressions, and financial mismanagement is highly suggestive of a specific neurodegenerative condition, but I need to review the MRI results from your recent scan to confirm the presence of characteristic atrophy before finalizing. DIAGNOSIS READY: Parkinson's Disease with Mild Cognitive Impairment (possibly progressing to Dementia with Lewy Bodies or Parkinson's Dementia).
